subject: HIPAA / BAA eligibility — post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jason Lee <jason.lee@healthcloud.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 25 May 2029 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: HIPAA / BAA eligibility — post-call recap & next steps

Jason — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

1) Scope and ask
- HealthCloud is evaluating Redwood Inference to power anonymized patient summarization for clinical workflows. Primary ask: confirm whether a BAA is available and which deployment options are eligible for PHI (fully PHI, limited PHI, or non-PHI).

2) What we confirmed on the call
- Redwood offers dedicated and private deployment modes that can be used for PHI workloads. Hosted/shared mode is not HIPAA-eligible.
- We are SOC 2 Type II compliant; we can share a redacted summary and SOC 2 report under an NDA.
- We support customer-managed KMS for key control in Private deployments and VPC peering for network isolation.

3) Outstanding items / next steps
- Marissa (me): circulate a short BAA eligibility matrix and SOC 2 summary (attached) — DONE in my follow up email.
- HealthCloud: confirm whether you need an on-prem or VPC/private deployment, and whether PHI will be full identifiers or tokenized downstream (this affects recommended architecture).
- HealthCloud Security: if you prefer, we can start the vendor security questionnaire; I can send the link and point Neha as our security lead.

Please reply with what deployment mode you expect to use and whether you want the security questionnaire started. If helpful, we can schedule a short follow-up with Neha and Dev to map the architecture.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments referenced: Redwood_BAA_eligibility_matrix.pdf, Redwood_SOC2-summary-2028.pdf
From: Jason Lee <jason.lee@healthcloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: HealthCloud Security <security@healthcloud.com>
Date: Sun, 26 May 2029 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HIPAA / BAA eligibility — post-call recap & next steps

Marissa — thanks for the recap. A couple quick clarifications from my side:

- Deployment mode: our default preference is Private (VPC) deployment in AWS — we want to keep data in our account and use our KMS. We may explore on-prem for selected customers, but start with VPC.
- PHI scope: the workload will process direct patient identifiers initially (names, MRNs) during ingestion, though downstream outputs will be de-identified.
- Questionnaire: yes, please send the vendor security questionnaire to our security team (cc'd).

Also: when you say Hosted/shared is not HIPAA-eligible, can you confirm whether there are any hybrid patterns (we keep storage on our side but use Redwood runtime)? We need to capture any limiting assumptions for architecture and cost.

— Jason
Jason Lee
Head of Product, HealthCloud
jason.lee@healthcloud.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jason Lee <jason.lee@healthcloud.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, HealthCloud Security <security@healthcloud.com>
Date: Sun, 26 May 2029 12:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HIPAA / BAA eligibility — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Jason — helpful details. Short answers inline and next actions:

- Private (VPC) + customer-managed KMS: fully supported and the recommended path for workloads that process direct identifiers. In this mode we can sign a BAA.

- Hybrid patterns: we have two common patterns:
  * VPC + Customer Storage: compute (Redwood runtime) runs in a private environment with network peering and customer-side S3/KMS for storage. This is supported and can be BAA-eligible depending on data flow.
  * Dedicated but hosted control plane: control plane may be hosted but customer data paths (ingest, object storage) remain in your account. This is possible but requires specific isolation controls — we'll route this to Neha for security gating.

- PHI handling boundaries: because you indicated identifiers will be present at ingest, we advise the Private (VPC) deployment with customer-managed KMS. For de-identification workflows, we can architect tokenization or masking in the ingestion pipeline; Dev can draft an architecture sketch.

Attachments: I attached two docs — Redwood_BAA_eligibility_matrix.pdf (quick table of eligible modes and constraints) and Redwood_SOC2-summary-2028.pdf (redacted summary). If you need the full SOC 2 report we'll need an NDA; we can get that to you quickly.

Next steps I suggest:
- Jason / Security: confirm you want us to start the vendor security questionnaire and provide any PO/Procure contacts (if needed).
- HealthCloud: confirm VPC region and whether customer-managed KMS is required.
- Dev/Neha: propose a 30-min architecture session next week to review flows and any additional controls (logging, audit export, retention) — Marissa to coordinate calendar.

Best —
Marissa

Hi Jason / HealthCloud Security — looping in from Redwood security. Per Marissa's notes, we can proceed with an initial vendor security questionnaire. Link below is our intake form; once you complete it, our team will share any outstanding evidence (SOC 2 full report under NDA, BAA template, network diagrams).

Vendor security questionnaire: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/healthcloud-vendor-security-questionnaire

A few quick notes for the questionnaire and timeline:
- Please indicate whether you will host object storage and KMS in your account (this affects evidence and control mappings).
- If you need the full SOC 2 report or penetration test evidence, we require an executed NDA (we can route a simple mutual NDA if you don't already have one).
- Once the questionnaire is submitted, expect a 3-5 business day turnaround for standard artifacts (redacted SOC 2 summary, BAA eligibility matrix). For SOC 2 full report or penetration test outputs, timeline is 5-10 business days pending approvals.

I'll assign an internal engineer (Dev) to coordinate the architecture session once you confirm region and KMS choice.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
